images.prompt:
Create exactly one premium photorealistic field-guide portrait of a mature Lab Pei (Labrador Retriever–Shar-Pei cross), using the attached creator-captioned adult cross photograph only as a private morphology reference. Make a new adult individual, new natural pose, new setting and new light. Do not reproduce the source dog Newly, the top-down camera, lawn, stone edge or composition. This adult source dog is not the named shelter dogs Georgie or Maree; do not transfer their age, identity or behavior to the generated individual. No pedigree, genetic percentage, measured age or source-tail cause claim.

Generate the original natively at exactly 1536 by 1024 pixels, landscape 3:2, fully opaque. Do not resize, crop, pad, stretch, extend or edit a differently sized image into this format. One dog only, full body, dog-eye viewpoint; comfortably inset both ears, all four feet and the entire tail. The adult dog should occupy about 60–65 percent of frame height, with at least 150 pixels of clear environment above its highest ear and at least 140 pixels of visible firm ground beneath its lowest paw; generous margins at both horizontal sides. Full environment remains visible. No tight headshot or oversized dog.

Morphology: preserve the reference's developed medium-large, sturdy but proportionate adult conformation: broad developed chest, substantial neck, moderate-length full trunk, strong hindquarters and a modest abdominal tuck. Short dense warm tan body coat, naturally folded/drop triangular ears, brown eyes, black nose and a broad proportionate muzzle with modest dark shading; softly folded forehead and realistic slightly loose face/neck skin, without exaggerated deep wrinkles. Keep the clear non-flat muzzle and the observed balanced head-to-body proportions. Do not replace this individual cross phenotype with a generic pure Labrador, extremely wrinkled heavy Shar-Pei, brachycephalic face or puppy. Retain the observed complete moderately long raised tail, starting visibly at the croup, curving outward in an open gentle arc with somewhat fuller terminal fur and a clearly separate freely outlined tip. No invented extra tail length, tightly coiled doughnut, oversized spitz plume, abrupt cut stump or tail hidden over the rump. Source-tail cause is unknown; preserve the visible course and proportion without diagnosing it.

Fresh art direction: a relaxed alert three-quarter standing pose facing slightly left, photographed at dog-eye level on a wide, level firm sandy-earth path beside a leafy neighborhood park meadow. Low grasses and a few oak trees sit well behind the dog, softly layered with gentle morning shade and restrained warm natural color. This is plausible companion-dog setting art direction, not a claim about breed origin, this source photograph's location or a shelter dog's history. Keep a balanced natural stance and a calm engaged expression, closed or slightly open mouth. All four complete anatomically coherent legs and separate grounded paws must be easily readable, with believable elbows, pasterns, hocks, toes, weight and contact shadows. No obstructing foreground plants, stones, toys or objects. Entire attached tail is clear of rump, legs and frame through its free endpoint. Natural believable canine anatomy; no duplicate or floating limbs. Fine short-coat texture. No collar, leash, harness, tags, people, text, graphic border, logo or watermark.
